title: Full Sail University Web Development: What Formal Training Actually Gave Me

cover.alt: Four connected model-making platforms represent starting, building, reviewing and presenting a project.

figures.title: The monthly project rhythm
figures.summary: The author describes a repeating four-stage course cycle.

items.label: Week 1
items.detail: Read the new topic's documentation and begin scaffolding.

items.label: Week 2
items.detail: Build the core implementation and debug the first obstacles.

items.label: Week 3
items.detail: Refine the project and prepare the presentation.

items.label: Week 4
items.detail: Deliver, present, receive feedback and move to the next topic.

figures.caption: A visual summary of the author's program experience, not a current university timetable.

figures.title: What transferred into later work
figures.summary: Compare each classroom habit with its later expression.

items.label: Start
items.detail: Class: begin a new project. Later: get an unfamiliar repository running.

items.label: Unblock
items.detail: Class: read documentation under a deadline. Later: investigate a deployment or service.

items.label: Present
items.detail: Class: demonstrate working software. Later: explain a project in a README or write-up.

items.label: Iterate
items.detail: Class: respond to instructor feedback. Later: respond to maintainers and reviewers.

figures.caption: The article's recurring habits, rather than a claim that any credential alone establishes engineering expertise.
